note: The StoreCatalog mirror remains the cipher-selection authority for its six stores. durableStores is the broader in-place-upgrade compatibility register: every process-owned durable authority names its owner, recovery class, format, write behavior, reconciliation, implementation, and evidence. HARDENING_REQUIRED rows are an explicit tempdoc-617 ratchet; the gate forbids adding an unnamed gap. Tempdoc 879 added two required per-row answers. pathVerification: LITERAL means ONE implementationSources file contains the string literal of every segment of the declared path - a union across several files does not count, because that made LITERAL satisfiable by adding an unrelated file that merely mentions the missing word; COMPOSED means the path is assembled at runtime, and pathVerificationNote must say by what. encryption: SEALED_BY_STORE_CIPHER = the StoreCatalog cipher seals it; UNSEALED_KEY_ROOT = it IS the key root and cannot be sealed by the key it holds; UNSEALED_EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY = the bytes belong to the user or an operator, not the app; UNSEALED_NO_JVM_CIPHER = Shell-owned, written by Rust with no reach to the JVM StoreCipher; UNSEALED_DERIVED_OS_DISK_ENCRYPTION = StoreCatalog's Framing.OPAQUE position, a derived/rebuildable store that does hold user-derived content in the clear and is covered by OS disk encryption only; UNSEALED_GAP = no structural reason, simply not sealed yet; NOT_APPLICABLE = there is nothing here worth sealing. UNSEALED_GAP, UNSEALED_DERIVED_OS_DISK_ENCRYPTION and NOT_APPLICABLE are all claims about what the bytes hold, so the gate requires an encryptionNote on each saying what the file actually contains - before 879 NOT_APPLICABLE was the one value nobody had to justify, and it was standing in for both 'nothing sensitive' and 'the user's own document text'. Known limit of the LITERAL check: it matches string literals, so it cannot tell a path constant from a same-named error-message label - a few rows (agent-runs, memories, conversations) are LITERAL-green via a CorruptDurableStoreException store label rather than a path constant, which means a rename of those directories could pass. Closing that needs the gate to recognise resolve(...)-shaped occurrences specifically; tracked in tempdoc 879. nonDurableWriteSites is the OTHER answer the coverage check accepts: a production source the write-site scanner flags that holds no durable state at all, so there is no recovery, upgrade or encryption policy to state for it. The bar is that every path it writes is scratch - process-scoped, regenerated on demand, and outside the data dir - so losing or deleting the file costs a recomputation and nothing else. It is not an escape hatch for a durable store whose row is inconvenient to write: if deleting the file would lose user-visible state, it belongs in durableStores. TempFileManager and WorkerProcessManager are JVM/OS temp scratch; ExtractionSandboxFactory writes one JVM temp file for the extraction child's startup probe and deletes it in the same method (tempdoc 885 item 14). DISCOVERY (wave-1 residue R1): the write-site scanner keys on write CALLS in code (scripts/governance/lib/persistence-write-scan.mjs strips comments, keeps literals), not on a "durable anchor" word appearing anywhere in the file text. The retired rule decided by reading English prose, which discovered ExtractionSandboxFactory via a javadoc sentence and missed ExtractionSandboxCommand's real argfile write. It over-discovers by design -- benchmarks, SSOT generators and the agent file tools all write to disk -- and each costs one honest nonDurableWriteSites line. nonDurableWriteSites entries are now { path, reason }: the classification is a claim, and every other row here justifies its claims. Six rows were added HARDENING_REQUIRED because the broadened scan found durable state no row owned: agent-history-markdown, ai-install-attempt-memory, gpl-eval-snapshot, gpl-stage-reports, llama-server-log and agent-user-document-operations. They are HARDENING_REQUIRED and not READY on purpose -- each names what IS established (owner, path, format, write mode) and marks its corruption policy NOT_YET_STATED rather than inventing one, because a READY row asserting an unverified recovery story is the false authority this register exists to prevent.
